prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Reform UK “Contract with You” (2024) — policies and costings only

Core pledges
- Freeze non‑essential immigration; stop small‑boat crossings via legal/operational changes.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000.
- Cut energy costs by scrapping green levies/Net Zero targets; expand domestic oil and gas.

Immigration
- Freeze non‑essential visas (healthcare as main exception).
- Detain and deport illegal entrants; offshore processing; bar asylum/citizenship if arriving from safe countries; no legal aid for non‑citizens.
- Immediate deportation of foreign criminals post‑sentence; potential citizenship withdrawal for crimes.
- Bar student dependants; restrict post‑study work to essential skills; close “fake” courses.
- Five‑year residency and employment to access benefits.
- Employer Immigration Tax: NI at 20% for foreign workers (exempt health/care and firms ≤5 staff). Claimed: £5–10bn savings + £4bn revenue pa.

Government spending/waste
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves to banks (claimed £35bn pa).
- 5% efficiency saving across departments without reducing front‑line services (claimed £50bn pa).
- Cut foreign aid by 50% (£6bn); reduce regulation; improve HMRC tax collection.

Economy – personal (cost ~£70bn pa)
- Personal allowance to £20k; higher rate from £70k.
- Cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap VAT on energy; remove environmental levies.
- Stamp Duty: 0% to £750k; 2% £750k–£1.5m; 4% over £1.5m.
- Reinstate VAT‑free tourist shopping.
- Inheritance Tax: 0% up to £2m; 20% above (charity alternative).

Economy – business (cost ~£18bn pa)
- No corporation tax on profits ≤£100k; main rate 25%→20%, then 15% (year 3).
- Abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high‑street SMEs; 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals; entrepreneurs’ tax to 5%.
- Planning reform; deregulation incl. employment law; tax simplification.

NHS (cost ~£17bn pa)
- Zero basic rate tax for frontline NHS and social care staff (3 years); expand UK medical training; student fee write‑off tied to service.
- Use independent/not‑for‑profit/overseas capacity; 20% tax relief on private health and insurance.
- Voucher guarantees: GP 3 days, consultant 3 weeks, operation 9 weeks; weekend theatres; reduce management; review PFI; charge for no‑shows; “Pharmacy First.”
- Public inquiry into excess deaths/vaccine harms.

Energy/Net Zero (claimed saving ~£30bn pa)
- Scrap Net Zero obligations and renewable subsidies (offset via equivalent taxes).
- Fast‑track North Sea and shale (trial), with local compensation.
- Accelerate SMRs and other technologies.

Policing (cost ~£3bn pa)
- +40,000 officers over 5 years; expanded stop and search; mandatory sentences for violent/knife/drug trafficking offences.
- Leadership/recruitment changes; reduce paperwork; phase out PCSOs; remove DEI roles; reform IOPC; revise College of Policing entry/fitness.

Justice (cost ~£2bn pa)
- Mandatory life for violent repeat offenders; budget to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; redefine hate crime; +10,000 prison places.
- Reforms on child grooming gangs, family court/maintenance, youth offender training.

Education (cost ~£5bn pa)
- Curriculum changes; restrict gender‑related practices in schools; single‑sex facilities.
- 20% tax relief on independent schooling; scrap interest on student loans; longer repayment; minimum entry standards; penalties for campus free‑speech breaches; more PRUs; optional 2‑year degrees.

Benefits (claimed saving ~£15bn pa)
- “Make work pay” via tax changes; training/apprenticeships; two‑strike job‑offer rule; face‑to‑face assessments (with exemptions).

Brexit/constitutional
- Repeal retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate TCA; limit EU defence links.
- Leave ECHR; reform Human Rights Act; reform Lords/civil service; restrict postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights.

Defence (cost ~£14bn pa)
- Spend 2.5% GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay review; Armed Forces Justice Bill; dedicated veterans department; recruit 30k; procurement/industry reforms; free education.

Housing (cost neutral)
- Fast‑track brownfield; social housing priority for locals; restore mortgage interest deductibility; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; leaseholder protections; construction tech.

Families (cost ~£8bn pa)
- Transferable marriage allowance (as finances allow); front‑load child benefit (ages 1–4); single‑sex spaces; child‑safe smartphones inquiry; review Online Safety Bill.

Transport/utilities (savings: £25bn one‑off; £5bn pa)
- Scrap remaining HS2; end ULEZ/LTNs; no bans on petrol/diesel; regional upgrades.
- Utilities: 50% public/50% UK pension‑fund ownership; cap standing charges; streamline infrastructure funding.

Agriculture (cost ~£2bn pa) and fisheries (cost ~£2bn pa)
- Increase farm budget to £3bn; replace climate‑linked subsidies; CMA pricing powers; “Buy British” targets; cut admin.
- Restrict foreign access/licensing; expand patrols; ban supertrawlers/pulse fishing; rebuild processing and fleets; sustainable management.

Pensions/social care
- Royal Commission; single funding stream; address offshore tax practices; pension system review; implement Mineworkers’ recommendations.

Funding (party claims)
- Potential savings ~£150bn pa + £10bn pa from assumed extra growth = £160bn pa.
- Total policy costs ~£141bn pa.
